title: DTC participant readiness scenarios
disclaimer: DTC-shaped, not DTC-certified. Scenarios tagged @inferred or @unknown rest on profile rows that DTCC has not published; results must be labelled accordingly.

scenarios.title: Smoke: the sandbox boots and reports the active profile
given: the sandbox server is started with profile dtc-stellar
scenarios.when: GET /v1/health
then: status 200
body.profile is dtc-stellar and body.lineage is [dtc-generic, dtc-stellar]
response carries the x-dtc-kit-disclaimer header

scenarios.title: A participant registers a wallet and it completes after OFAC screening and allowlisting
given: participant SBX-9001 with a service account
no wallets registered
scenarios.when: the participant POSTs /v1/wallets for an internal wallet, then simulated time advances 60 s
then: registration response status is Processing
afterwards the wallet status is Completed
the wallet is allowlisted on the sandbox ledger

scenarios.title: A caller that is not a DTC Participant cannot register a wallet
given: a service account that belongs to no participant
scenarios.when: it POSTs /v1/wallets
then: status 403 with code NOT_A_PARTICIPANT
no wallet record is created

scenarios.title: An OFAC failure leaves the wallet Failed Compliance, not allowlisted and barred from conversion orders
given: a client of SBX-9004 on the sandbox sanctions list (SBX-SDN-0001)
scenarios.when: the participant registers that client's wallet and then creates a to-token conversion order
then: wallet status becomes Failed Compliance
onChainAllowlisted is false
the order is Declined with reasonCode WALLET_FAILED_COMPLIANCE

scenarios.title: The registry accepts any address text; DTC does not validate it
given: a participant
scenarios.when: it registers a wallet whose address is not a well-formed address for the chosen ledger
then: registration is accepted (202)
the participant, not the registry, bears the consequence (precheck reports the address as unusable on the ledger)

scenarios.title: A client wallet must carry a client identifier that ties it to a client record
given: participant SBX-9002 with clients C-BIRCH-001..003
scenarios.when: it registers a wallet of kind client without clientId, then with an unknown clientId, then with C-BIRCH-001
then: the first two are rejected with 422
the third is accepted
the wallets CSV lists the clientId

scenarios.title: A transfer to an unregistered address is refused
given: a funded Completed wallet
an address that is not in the registry
scenarios.when: the holder transfers 1 token to the unregistered address
then: precheck returns DEST_NOT_REGISTERED
the transfer fails and the balance is unchanged
on a chain adapter the failure is a ledger-level rejection, not only a registry check

scenarios.title: A transfer between two Completed wallets succeeds
given: two Completed wallets, the first holding 10 tokens
scenarios.when: the first transfers 4 tokens to the second
then: balances are 6 and 4
both Activity rows exist (Payment, Payment Received)

scenarios.title: A transfer to a Failed Compliance wallet is refused
given: a wallet in Failed Compliance
a funded Completed wallet
scenarios.when: a transfer to the Failed Compliance wallet is attempted
then: precheck returns DEST_FAILED_COMPLIANCE
no tokens move

scenarios.title: A transfer to a wallet whose DTC authorisation has not landed on-chain is refused
given: the participant created a trustline but DTC has not yet authorised it
scenarios.when: a funded wallet transfers to that address
then: precheck returns DEST_STATUS_NOT_COMPLETED
ledger-level failure is 'balance is deauthorized'

scenarios.title: A to-token conversion order mints whole tokens 1:1 into a Completed wallet
given: a Completed wallet and 100 book-entry shares
scenarios.when: the participant creates a to-token order for 100 and time advances 15 min
then: order status goes Processing then Completed
wallet balance is 100 tokens
classic balance is reduced by 100 shares
total supply equals total book-entry shares converted

scenarios.title: A fractional conversion quantity is declined, not rounded
given: a Completed wallet
scenarios.when: the participant creates a to-token order with quantity "1.5"
then: status 422 with reasonCode FRACTIONAL_QUANTITY
no order is created in Processing

scenarios.title: A to-book-entry conversion burns the tokens and credits the classic position
given: a wallet holding 100 tokens
scenarios.when: the participant creates a to-book-entry order for 40
then: wallet balance is 60
classic position increases by 40
supply decreases by 40

scenarios.title: An on-chain revert during conversion automatically reverses the ledger changes
given: a to-token order whose mint transaction is made to fail on-chain (for example the destination trustline is deauthorised)
scenarios.when: the order is processed
then: order status is Failed
classic position is restored exactly
no token supply was created

scenarios.title: A cross-network move is a burn on one chain and a mint on the other, only inside processing hours
given: two sandbox ledgers
simulated clock at Saturday 10:00 ET, then Monday 10:00 ET
scenarios.when: a cross-network move is requested at each time
then: Saturday: refused CROSS_NETWORK_OUTSIDE_HOURS
Monday: burn on source, mint on destination, supply conserved across both
a same-network transfer works on Saturday

scenarios.title: A Delivery Order Chill blocks outbound transfers until it is released
given: a funded Completed wallet and a Completed counterparty
scenarios.when: DTC applies delivery-order-chill, a transfer is attempted, DTC releases, the transfer is retried
then: during the chill the transfer is refused SOURCE_RESTRICTED
after release it succeeds
the label on the refusal is @inferred (control effects are our reading)

scenarios.title: A Global Lock blocks both inbound and outbound activity
given: a funded Completed wallet
scenarios.when: DTC applies global-lock and both an inbound and an outbound transfer are attempted
then: outbound refused SOURCE_RESTRICTED
inbound refused DEST_RESTRICTED

scenarios.title: Releasing a control restores the status the wallet had before it
given: a Completed wallet
scenarios.when: DTC applies a Compliance Lock from the sanctions feed and later releases it
then: status moves Completed -> Compliance Lock -> Completed
on-chain restriction is applied then removed (effects restrict / unrestrict)

scenarios.title: The DTC override moves tokens without the holder's signature
given: two Completed wallets, the first holding 10 tokens, whose holder key is unavailable to the test
scenarios.when: DTC ops force-transfer 10 tokens from the first to the second, reason erroneous
then: balances are 0 and 10
no signature of the first wallet's holder was used
the second wallet must be a Registered Wallet or the force transfer is refused DEST_NOT_REGISTERED

scenarios.title: On a classic asset a force transfer is one atomic transaction: clawback plus issuer payment
given: a testnet asset with AUTH_REQUIRED, AUTH_REVOCABLE and AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED set before any trustline exists
holder A with 10 tokens, holder B with an authorised trustline
scenarios.when: the adapter plans a force transfer A -> B of 10 and it is submitted with throwaway testnet keys ; variant: B's trustline is deauthorised
then: main case: one transaction containing [clawback(A,10), payment(issuer->B,10)]; A=0, B=10, supply unchanged
variant: the whole transaction fails, A still holds 10 (this is why one transaction is required)
result is labelled @unknown: DTCC has not said this is the mechanism

scenarios.title: SEP-57 forced_transfer from a frozen address: record what happens
given: a SEP-57 token on testnet
address A frozen with set_address_frozen, and a variant with A partially frozen, and a variant with the token paused
scenarios.when: the operator calls forced_transfer(A, B, amount)
then: no pass/fail assertion: the outcome of each variant is recorded as a fixture with provenance
the capability matrix cell for force-transfer is updated from the observation

scenarios.title: A force transfer, clawback and mint are distinguishable on-chain from an ordinary transfer
given: one ordinary transfer and one admin action per adapter on testnet
scenarios.when: the events of both transactions are decoded
then: record the topic layout of each; assert nothing beyond 'decodable'
capability cell admin-events-distinguishable is updated

scenarios.title: Every root-wallet use is counted for the quarterly SEC report
given: three force transfers (two erroneous, one stolen) in one quarter
scenarios.when: the root-wallet-uses summary is requested for that quarter
then: total is 3, by reason {erroneous: 2, stolen: 1}
a force transfer in the next quarter is not counted

scenarios.title: Position capture at 20:00 ET includes tokens held then and excludes tokens converted earlier
given: a record date in winter and one in summer (DST)
wallet W holds 100 tokens at 19:59 ET and converts 30 to book entry at 20:01 ET
scenarios.when: DTC captures positions for each record date
then: capture instant is 20:00 America/New_York (01:00Z winter+1d, 00:00Z summer+1d)
W is captured with 100 tokens
a conversion completed before 20:00 reduces the captured amount

scenarios.title: For an unsupported event a token converted to book entry before the record date is not captured and not re-tokenised
given: an event DTC does not support on tokens
a holder converts to book entry the day before the record date
scenarios.when: the record date passes
then: the holder's tokens are absent from the token capture
no automatic re-tokenisation occurs after the event

scenarios.title: One consolidated cash credit is allocated to client sub-ledgers pro rata to their captured tokens
given: participant SBX-9002 with clients C-BIRCH-001..003 holding 50, 30 and 20 tokens across five wallets at capture
a single credit of 100003 cents
scenarios.when: the reconciliation allocates the credit
then: allocation uses largest remainder with ties broken by client id, so it is deterministic
each client's share is within 1 cent of exact pro rata
internal (house) wallets are allocated to the house sub-ledger

scenarios.title: Allocated amounts sum exactly to the credit received: no cent lost or created
given: property test: random holder sets (1..10000 wallets) and credits (0..10^12 cents)
scenarios.when: the allocation runs
then: sum of allocations equals the credit, always
no negative allocation
same input in any order gives byte-identical output

scenarios.title: At maturity the tokens are burned and the cash credit equals principal
given: a maturity event for a sandbox Treasury; record date is the business day before maturity (inferred in SC-023, not asserted here)
scenarios.when: DTC pays the event
then: token supply goes to zero
one credit per participant to the classic account
interest events leave the tokens in place

scenarios.title: A credit that differs from the participant's expectation is flagged CREDIT_MISMATCH and not allocated silently
given: an expected credit computed from the participant's own capture
DTC credits 1 cent less
scenarios.when: the reconciliation runs
then: case state is Disputed with disputeCode CREDIT_MISMATCH
no allocation is posted until a human resolves it

scenarios.title: DTC cannot authorise a trustline that does not exist yet
given: a funded testnet account with no trustline to the asset
scenarios.when: the adapter's allowlist-add plan is submitted
then: the transaction fails (no trustline)
precheck reports DEST_NOT_REGISTERED until the participant creates the trustline and DTC authorises it

scenarios.title: A contract (C) address as a Registered Wallet: record what each adapter does
given: a deployed test contract (a minimal smart account or escrow)
scenarios.when: SAC: set_authorized on the contract address then a transfer to it ; SEP-57: add the contract to the identity registry / allowlist then a transfer to it
then: no pass/fail: record whether each step is possible and the exact error otherwise
the answer is NOT evidence about what DTC will allow; it bounds what the token side can do

scenarios.title: A classic asset or SAC cannot reject a fractional amount at ledger level
given: an authorised holder with 10 tokens (7 decimals)
scenarios.when: the holder pays 0.5 tokens to another authorised holder
then: the payment succeeds on-chain (documenting the limitation)
the sandbox precheck still reports FRACTIONAL_QUANTITY, so enforcement is registry-side only

scenarios.title: A contract token deployed with decimals 0 represents only whole tokens
given: a SEP-57 token deployed with decimals = 0
scenarios.when: decimals() is read and a transfer of 1 and of the smallest unit are made
then: decimals() returns 0
the smallest transferable unit is one share
wallet display of the balance is recorded (wallets may assume decimals)

scenarios.title: Wallet vendor: the custody stack signs classic trustline operations and a Soroban auth entry, and shows a control action clearly
given: a vendor test environment with a testnet vault (vendor supplies access; the kit never holds keys)
scenarios.when: the vendor stack is driven to: create a trustline, sign a SEP-41 transfer auth entry, display a forced_transfer / SetTrustLineFlags request for approval
then: each capability is reported supported / not supported / not testable, with the evidence
the result feeds readiness-pack/wallet-vendor-matrix.md; no vendor is named in a pass/fail without its consent (G-OUTREACH)

scenarios.title: Sub-ledger deposits can be attributed with muxed IDs where the stack supports them
given: one funded account and three muxed IDs for clients C-BIRCH-001..003
scenarios.when: classic payments are sent to each muxed address
then: the deposit detector attributes each payment to the right client ID
record which wallet/custody stacks surface the mux ID

scenarios.title: Reconcile 10,000 wallets against a HoldersSnapshot within the time budget
given: a synthetic HoldersSnapshot of 10,000 holders (shape owned by holders-at-ledger, not redefined here)
a participant ledger mapping 10,000 wallets to 500 clients
scenarios.when: reconciliation allocates one credit
then: completes within 1,000 ms (budget set from measurement on 2026-11-08: 91-134 ms on the 4-core build machine, Node 24.18; see SC035_BUDGET_MS)
output is identical to the small-case allocation rules
